subject: Literature
title: China's Cultural Revolution and Literary Destruction
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on China's Cultural Revolution and Literary Destruction.

hook.text: During China's Cultural Revolution, Red Guards raided homes and burned any book that was not by Mao Zedong.

buildup.text: From 1966 to 1976, classical Chinese literature, foreign novels, and religious texts were systematically destroyed.

discovery.text: Intellectuals were publicly humiliated, sent to labor camps, or killed for owning forbidden books.

twist.text: Some families buried books in their gardens or hid them in walls, preserving fragments of a literary culture under siege.

climax.text: The Cultural Revolution showed that totalitarian regimes attack literature because stories carry the memory of freedom.

punchline.text: They buried books like seeds waiting for a safer season.

quiz.question: How did some Chinese families preserve banned books during the Cultural Revolution?
options: They donated them to underground libraries
They buried them in gardens or hid them in walls
They memorized and destroyed the physical copies
